newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PAL workers strike, 21 flights cancelled.
newsitem.headline: PAL workers strike, 21 flights cancelled.

text.p: Workers at Philippine Airlines (PAL) went on strike over pay demands on Wednesday, forcing the airline to cancel eight international and 13 domestic flights, the airline said.

Hundreds of PAL ground personnel mounted pickets at Manila's domestic and international airports hours after President Fidel Ramos refused to intervene in the row despite warnings a walkout might embarrass the country ahead of next month's APEC summit.
Ramos, who had billed the November 25 summit of the APEC (Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation) forum as an event for which "we...must put on our best face," said he was not a labour arbiter.

The strike by the 9,000-strong PAL Employees Association (PALEA), involving ground and maintenance crews and other rank and file, delayed the departures of a Cathay Pacific Airways plane and a Qantas flight, airport sources said.
PAL crew provide catering and cargo services to several foreign airlines, including Singapore Airlines, Japan Airlines and Cathay, PALEA national secretary Jose Penas III said.
"Philippine Airlines management...is saddened by the decision of the PAL Employees Association to defy the law by staging an illegal strike early tonight," the airline said in a statement.
The employees walked out despite an appeal from the labour department that a strike before the APEC summit would embarrass the country.
The strike was the third to hit the financially-troubled national carrier in two years. PALEA struck twice in 1994, the first stoppage lasting a day and the second nine days.
PALEA and two other unions representing pilots and cabin crew on Tuesday urged Ramos to help avert the strike.
"I passed (the union request) immediately to the (labour department) because I should not be a labour arbiter," Ramos told a news conference.
There was no indication the pilots and cabin crew unions were involved in the walkout.

The three unions are asking for negotiations on a new wage package worth 3.2 billion pesos ($121 million) over the next two years. PAL has rejected the package and instead offered to sell PAL shares worth 477 million pesos ($18.15 million) at five pesos (19 cents) per share to employees.

"The stock offering will partially meet the cash component of the economic benefits demanded by the three PAL labour unions even while the airline is cash-strapped and continues to incur losses at approximately 3.0 million pesos ($114,133) a day that could reach more than one billion pesos ($38 million) by the end of the current fiscal year," the company said.
PAL has incurred losses in the past several years due to high operating expenses and cutthroat competition on international routes.
